name: VNET DC Digitalis
notes: VNET's flagship Tier III colocation data centre opened 2014 at Trnavska cesta in the wider centre of Bratislava, ~3000 m2, four redundant geographically independent fibre routes with >100 Gbit/s capacity and rental of dark fibre. VNET operates three data centres in Bratislava (Forbes profile). No public MW capacity.

name: SWAN Data Centre
notes: SWAN, a major Slovak telecom/ICT operator headquartered in Bratislava, offers data centre/colocation services (server housing, cloud, backup) per its official site. Exact DC address and capacity are not published.

name: Slovak Telekom Data Centre (Bratislava)
notes: Official page: DC located ~1 km from Bratislava centre, 5 km from airport, 80 km from Vienna, with UPS and doubled motor generators for uninterrupted supply. Data Center Catalog lists several Slovak Telekom sites in Bratislava: DC Jarosova, SHC II, SHC III and a generic 'Slovak Telekom DataCenter' entry. Capacity not published.

name: Orange Tech Park Data Centre
notes: Modern operator data centre at Orange Tech Park in Bratislava, built to international standards with careful siting (flood-safe, away from airport approach and heavy industry); Orange sells 'Virtual Data Centre' cloud services from it. No public MW capacity.

name: Towercom Datacentrum (Kamzik)
notes: Colocation DC in the premises of the Kamzik TV transmitter in Bratislava; designed to Tier III criteria, 480 m2 technology space, powered by two 1250 kVA transformers (N+1) with rotary UPS and NZ2 Phoenix Zeppelin diesel energy centre; INERGEN fire suppression; connectivity to SIX and SITEL peering. capacity_mw derived from 2x1250 kVA connected transformers.

name: Perpetuus DC / DCP1
notes: Purpose-built two-storey DC at Devinska Nova Ves, Bratislava suburb (Istrijska 26); Tier III, 3.5 MW electrical input on 2x22 kV per WebSupport (which runs its production infrastructure there; Inflect lists 2.5 MW total power capacity). WebSupport keeps backups in a second, geolocated Bratislava DC. One of the largest third-party data centres in Slovakia per Tariff Consultancy.

name: Datacube Data Centre
notes: Colocation DC at Kopcianska, Petrzalka (Bratislava); described as one of the largest third-party data centre facilities in Slovakia (Tariff Consultancy market study). Previously hosted NASES state systems (one floor) for the government cloud. Data Center Catalog also lists the related 'Datahouse Kopcianska' site. No public MW capacity.

name: GTS Slovakia DC
notes: Legacy carrier data centre of GTS Slovakia (acquired by Deutsche Telekom and integrated into the Slovak Telekom environment). Listed in Data Center Catalog as a Slovak facility; address/capacity not published there - likely Bratislava.

name: NASES State Data Centre (Government Cloud)
developer: NASES (National Agency for Network and Electronic Services)
notes: The state (NASES) operates two data centres serving the Govnet government network and slovensko.sk portal; since end 2021 one is hosted in SPP (Slovensky plynarensky priemysel) premises in Bratislava, the other previously in Datacube (Kopcianska). The state also evaluated buying the Rattajova building in Petrzalka for a new state data centre. No public MW capacity.

name: Platon Chemtech Data Centre
notes: Small operator-run server room 'Chemtech' (~36 m2) located ~400 m from SIX (Slovak Internet eXchange) in Bratislava; hosting/colocation provider. Minor facility, included for completeness.

name: SIS new data centre (planned)
notes: The Slovak Intelligence Service announced plans (Strategy 2025-2032, reported Nov 2025) to build a new data centre and modernise technical intelligence; location not disclosed - assigned to Bratislava (SIS headquarters) for coverage. Announced/planned stage, no capacity published.

name: Slovak Telekom DC Tajov
notes: Hardened bunker-type data centre at Tajov 1, 976 34 Tajov (Banska Bystrica region): autonomous operation for min. 6 days, resistant to nuclear/chemical/bacteriological attack, seismic up to 7 Richter, EMP, floods; power and data connectivity from three directions; doubled cooling/backup/motor-generator technology. Operator description via tdc@telekom.sk. Capacity not published.

name: Slovak Telekom DC Kosice
notes: Data centre within an existing T-Com telecom building at Polska 4, 043 06 Kosice; two-way energy connection with UPS and doubled motor generator, EFS/EAS and automated fire protection; housing services (cages, racks, footprints, dedicated servers). Capacity not published.

name: Slovak Telekom DC Bzenov
notes: Hardened bunker data centre at Bzenov 082 42 (Presov district): 72h autonomy, three independent HV connections, 2x825 kVA diesel generators, 50,000 l fuel, own water source, sited away from flood/industrial/communication hazards; rack/cage housing services. Capacity not published.

name: Geothermal Park Presov-Lubotice data centre (planned)
notes: Developer promotes a next-generation data centre opportunity within the Geothermal Park Presov - Lubotice project (confirmed geothermal resource ~140-150 C, valid EIA decision, ~8.5 MWe geothermal power plant planned, site on Via Carpatia axis near Presov): absorption chillers driven by geothermal heat could cut cooling electricity to 5-10% of conventional systems and push PUE toward 1.2. Concept/announced stage; DC capacity not specified.
